_doc: Declares this repo's legal/consent surfaces per cais-shared-services/REGULATORY_INCLUSIONS.md. Every inclusion must be default, customised, or not-applicable WITH A REASON — silence is not acceptance.

operator._doc: Trigger A. Kira is a CAS-owned product, so it carries OUR canonical identity (portfolio-manifest.yaml `shared:`). A white-label or distributor product would carry theirs — that is the gate, and this is the case where the default is correct rather than assumed.

review._doc: Best-fit pages written from what the product actually does. Not legal advice — the same standing caveat lib/terms.ts already carries.
review.note: A lawyer should review before real volume, together with the introducer agreement (BROKER_CHANNEL_BUILD_STATE guardrails). Not blocking today: Kira is CAS-owned, so unlike BucketLyst there is no third party whose entity we are guessing at.

privacy.note: lib/privacy.ts, mirroring lib/terms.ts so the two versions and dates can be reasoned about together. Three sections that could not have come from a template: what an INTRODUCER can see (status only — enforced by introducer_owner_projection in SQL, so it is stated as fact not promise), what Kira remembers (distilled summary, per-account, deletable without closing the account), and the valuation figures (turnover and profit, collected before an account even exists).

terms.note: lib/terms.ts. Version recorded at signup acceptance, so it is answerable which wording a given user agreed to.

voice.note: Vendor consent modal (ElevenLabs), unmodified. The package exposes NO consent-text configuration, so overriding it needs a direct API PATCH or a package addition. Mitigated by privacy §4, which states the same thing in our words. The naive-tester finding was that product copy CONTRADICTED the modal ('what you tell Kira stays between you and your business'); the privacy policy now reconciles it — the data stays with the account, and the processing by ElevenLabs is stated plainly rather than left to the vendor notice alone.

ip_ack.reason: Users do not create or share content built on third-party IP. What they produce is their own business information, and the terms already state it remains theirs.

cookies.reason: Session cookie only, strictly necessary to keep a signed-in user signed in. No analytics, no advertising, no cross-site tracking — disclosed in the privacy policy rather than gated behind a banner. Re-declare the moment any analytics is added.

automated_decisions._doc: Privacy Act APP 1.7/1.8 (POLA Act 2024), commencing 10 December 2026: a privacy policy must describe the kinds of personal information used in automated decision-making, the kinds of decisions made, and broadly how the process works — where a decision could reasonably be expected to SIGNIFICANTLY AFFECT the individual's rights or interests. OAIC gains infringement-notice powers, penalties to $330,000.
automated_decisions.note: Section 'What Kira works out on her own'. Disclosed although the threshold is probably NOT met — see assessment.

assessment.threshold: Probably out of scope. The rule targets decisions an organisation makes ABOUT a person that change what they can have (credit refused, application screened out, claim declined). Kira's automated outputs are about the OWNER'S OWN BUSINESS, shown to the owner, and grant or deny him nothing.
surfaces_reviewed: lib/valuation/model.ts computeValuation — deterministic SDE arithmetic, no model in the path. An estimate, not a decision.
lib/genome/private.ts isOwnerPrivate — deterministic matcher withholding the owner's position from the buyer handover. Real consequence, but made in his favour.
memory distillation — chooses what is retained; readable and deletable by him.
declined_because / refusal classification — internal governance, not a decision about the user.
Genome coverage bands + Transferability /100 — score the business, shown only to him.
assessment.disclosed_anyway_because: The product collects turnover, profit and frequently that the owner has not told his staff or family — the policy itself calls this the most sensitive information most owners will type into anything. Declining to describe the automation on the grounds that a threshold is arguably unmet is a technicality argued at the reader least likely to extend credit. It is also cheap: the honest disclosure is that nothing automated sets his price, access or standing.
open_for_legal_review: Whether the small-business exemption applies to Global Buildtech Australia Pty Ltd (turnover under $3M, absent an exception). NOT DETERMINED — it decides whether this is mandatory or good practice, and it is an operator fact, not a code fact.
Whether the valuation, being an estimate the owner acts on, could be argued to 'directly support' a decision that significantly affects him.
assessment.reassess_when: Any automated process begins to decide something ABOUT a user — pricing, eligibility, ranking against other customers, or anything reported to a third party. The privacy section commits to changing before that ships.

automated_decisions.confirmed_by: Dennis McMahon, 2026-08-08 — pending the legal review already recorded in `review` above
